items.title: Mrs. Francis Oliver Interview, 1969-05-10
items.q: his friends wanted to call me Little Jelly, and he didn't want that. He'd say, her name's Mimi. ... And he kept me away from his friends.

ctx.x: Well, there were some of the musicians around Chicago that I've talked to, like Maddie Dominick and Roy Palmer, a trombonist. Mm-hmm. And Lee Collins, who's now dead, a coronet player. They made records with your brother. With Jelly, yes. Around that time, 1924 and 23.

And then, you see, his friends wanted to call me Little Jelly, and he didn't want that. He'd say, her name's Mimi. And you see, they wouldn't think of my name. They'd say, all right, Little Jelly, so-and-so. And he kept me away from his friends. He didn't want me to be nicknamed Little Jelly. No. Was he much taller? He didn't seem much taller than you. He's six feet three. Six feet three. Yes, sir. He's taller than my tallest uncle. This isn't very good of him either. No, no. He was six feet old.
They tell there. That was the last picture taken of him. Mm-hmm. And I'd never seen it before that book came out there.
